headline: Petrol bomb hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura; police investigating incident
summary: Unidentified individuals threw a petrol bomb and a cocktail at the gate of the former national cricket captain and MP's residence on Wednesday night. Police have been deployed for security.
details: Unidentified miscreants hurled a petrol bomb and a cocktail at the gate of former Awami League MP and Bangladesh national cricket team captain Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura. The incident occurred on Wednesday night at his residence in Keshab More.

Police reported that an explosive-like object was thrown and set on fire targeting the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the house. The fire extinguished quickly without significant damage.
A team from Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene after receiving the news. Police have since been deployed to ensure security at the property.

Authorities have not yet identified the perpetrators or confirmed the exact motive behind the incident. An investigation is currently underway to determine the true cause and the nature of the thrown objects.

headline_marked: [[Rabindranath Tagore's 85th death anniversary]] observed today, honoring his immense legacy
headline: Rabindranath Tagore's 85th death anniversary observed today, honoring his immense legacy
summary: The literary giant, who composed two national anthems and won the Nobel Prize in Literature, passed away on August 7, 1941, according to the Gregorian calendar. Bangladesh observes his death anniversary on Sraban 22.
details: Today marks the 85th death anniversary of Biswakabi Rabindranath Tagore. While he passed away on August 7, 1941, at the age of 80, Bangladesh observes his death anniversary on Sraban 22 of the Bangla calendar.
Born on May 7, 1861 (Baishakh 25, 1268 Bangla) at the Jorasanko mansion in Calcutta, Tagore was the youngest of 13 surviving children of Debendranath Tagore and Sarada Devi.

Known as the "Bard of Bengal," he composed over 2,000 songs, forming the distinct genre of "Rabindra Sangeet." His prolific literary career, spanning nearly seven decades, also included eight novels, 84 short stories, and countless poems.

Rabindranath Tagore made history in 1913 by becoming the first non-European to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. His profound impact is further highlighted by two of his compositions, "Amar Shonar Bangla" and "Jana Gana Mana," being chosen as the national anthems for Bangladesh and India, respectively.
caption:
Today marks the 85th death anniversary of Rabindranath Tagore, the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature. His legacy includes composing the national anthems for both Bangladesh and India.

Today marks the 85th death anniversary of Biswakabi Rabindranath Tagore. While he passed away on August 7, 1941, at the age of 80, Bangladesh observes his death anniversary on Sraban 22 of the Bangla calendar.

Born on May 7, 1861 (Baishakh 25, 1268 Bangla) at the Jorasanko mansion in Calcutta, Tagore was the youngest of 13 surviving children of Debendranath Tagore and Sarada Devi.

Known as the "Bard of Bengal," he composed over 2,000 songs, forming the distinct genre of "Rabindra Sangeet." His prolific literary career, spanning nearly seven decades, also included eight novels, 84 short stories, and countless poems.

Rabindranath Tagore made history in 1913 by becoming the first non-European to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. His profound impact is further highlighted by two of his compositions, "Amar Shonar Bangla" and "Jana Gana Mana," being chosen as the national anthems for Bangladesh and India, respectively.
